definition: Storing cached keys/values in 8-bit or 4-bit, multiplying how many concurrent long-context requests fit in memory, usually with negligible quality impact at 8-bit.
details: Storing cached keys/values in 8-bit or 4-bit, multiplying how many concurrent long-context requests fit in memory, usually with negligible quality impact at 8-bit.

explainer.lead: KV cache quantization stores attention cache entries at 8-bit or 4-bit precision instead of full precision. This multiplies how many concurrent long-context requests fit in memory.

tiers.eli5: Instead of keeping every past word in a bulky notebook, you jot them down in shorthand, so many more conversations fit on the same shelf.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to cut memory when serving long-context models, and at 8-bit the quality impact is usually negligible. Dropping to 4-bit is a bigger memory win but a riskier trade against output quality.
tiers.paperLevel: Cached key and value vectors are stored in 8-bit or 4-bit representations rather than their native precision; the reported quality impact is usually negligible at 8-bit. No formal bound is given beyond that.

explainer.example: Serving long-context requests, moving the KV cache from full precision to 8-bit lets more concurrent requests share the same GPU memory.
